$$

$$

Therefore, only $B$ and $C$ are in row echelon form." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-848d2bf5-7181-5403-afac-d10425ef5d8c"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-848d2bf5-7181-5403-afac-d10425ef5d8c" :answer-field/id #uuid "848d2bf5-7181-5403-afac-d10425ef5d8c" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-3fd4fdcb-52a1-577b-9cee-a9fa9d18334b" :answer-field/choices ["answer-e9c227b1-80fa-5ed1-8fcb-7bbadbc92d9f" "answer-12f4ffe3-c54b-5dec-af7e-f3eb29c5efac" "answer-0bcbaf3a-7d79-5c34-9970-8e30a0164f3d" "answer-3fd4fdcb-52a1-577b-9cee-a9fa9d18334b" "answer-42122353-59f4-5dee-9867-47f69bf794e2"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e9c227b1-80fa-5ed1-8fcb-7bbadbc92d9f" :answer/id #uuid "e9c227b1-80fa-5ed1-8fcb-7bbadbc92d9f" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "$A$ and $B$ only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-12f4ffe3-c54b-5dec-af7e-f3eb29c5efac" :answer/id #uuid "12f4ffe3-c54b-5dec-af7e-f3eb29c5efac" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "$A$ and $C$ only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0bcbaf3a-7d79-5c34-9970-8e30a0164f3d" :answer/id #uuid "0bcbaf3a-7d79-5c34-9970-8e30a0164f3d" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "$A,$ $B,$ and $C$" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3fd4fdcb-52a1-577b-9cee-a9fa9d18334b" :answer/id #uuid "3fd4fdcb-52a1-577b-9cee-a9fa9d18334b" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "$B$ and $C$ only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-42122353-59f4-5dee-9867-47f69bf794e2" :answer/id #uuid "42122353-59f4-5dee-9867-47f69bf794e2" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "$B$ only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-17d0a606-b191-57ce-bda5-cb6bdd31b9a8" :question/id #uuid "17d0a606-b191-57ce-bda5-cb6bdd31b9a8" :question/math-academy-id "q-42373" :question/problem "Consider the matrix $A$ given below.

A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,⟶\,[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

The other options will not give us a matrix in row echelon form." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-c9772538-fd34-5f2a-b5f8-a7d295110074"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-c9772538-fd34-5f2a-b5f8-a7d295110074" :answer-field/id #uuid "c9772538-fd34-5f2a-b5f8-a7d295110074" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-2231485a-d292-515f-b51b-91f31ecd0efe" :answer-field/choices ["answer-a5bcd7de-6ec8-511e-9e85-d25e1afb7c50" "answer-dbd6ae2c-f7e4-5a2b-9120-ea5f2f442053" "answer-82eb2341-c973-51c4-a691-9aab4038100d" "answer-2231485a-d292-515f-b51b-91f31ecd0efe" "answer-0e03e0f4-f6d8-5e5e-be1b-2065040084b9"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a5bcd7de-6ec8-511e-9e85-d25e1afb7c50" :answer/id #uuid "a5bcd7de-6ec8-511e-9e85-d25e1afb7c50" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "${a}_{32}$ and ${a}_{22}$ only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-dbd6ae2c-f7e4-5a2b-9120-ea5f2f442053" :answer/id #uuid "dbd6ae2c-f7e4-5a2b-9120-ea5f2f442053" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "${a}_{32}$ and ${a}_{43}$ only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-82eb2341-c973-51c4-a691-9aab4038100d" :answer/id #uuid "82eb2341-c973-51c4-a691-9aab4038100d" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "${a}_{32}$ only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-2231485a-d292-515f-b51b-91f31ecd0efe" :answer/id #uuid "2231485a-d292-515f-b51b-91f31ecd0efe" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "${a}_{32}$, ${a}_{43}$ and ${a}_{44}$ only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-0e03e0f4-f6d8-5e5e-be1b-2065040084b9" :answer/id #uuid "0e03e0f4-f6d8-5e5e-be1b-2065040084b9" :answer/type :answer.type/text :answer/value "${a}_{43}$ only" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186130339 :tutorial/content "Consider the following matrices:
![](images/10/1074870d255109821b5f36eb517f22531efbd8f5069f05c3de3f111b38befd02.svg)

The first non-zero entry on each row (from left to right) is called the **leading entry** of that row.

- In the matrix $A,$ the leading entries are $a_{11}=2,$ $a_{22}=3,$ $a_{32}=1,$ and $a_{43}=5.$

- In the matrix $B,$ the leading entries are $b_{11}=1,$ $b_{22}=3,$ $b_{33}=-2,$ and $b_{44}=2.$ The $5$th row has no leading entry.

The leading entries are highlighted below.

![](images/6b/6b1d99269c847f7c6bc0558da347fb300dba5fa6caf373cd1ed5cc5ebacb1649.svg)" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186130380 :tutorial/content "Let's consider our matrices $A$ and $B$ once more, with the leading entries highlighted.

![](images/af/af61f32297e248ab9989ba59ea6c9bda2f99efe19d25df525fef916617843a32.svg)

We say that a matrix is in **row echelon form** if it satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

Here, $B$ is in row echelon form since both conditions are satisfied. However, $A$ is not in row echelon form since condition II is violated: the leading entry of the third row $(a_{32}={\color{red}1})$ is placed just below the leading entry of the second row $(a_{22}=3).$

Generally speaking, row echelon form means that we have *stairs* where each step (represented by a leading entry $\bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{\large\ast}$) has a height of $1.$

![](images/67/67f83c454e59d16ae80cf67a19b19f968182251a2e5d1b405e2c422e0313d5b7.png)

Finally, an *augmented* matrix is in row echelon form if the coefficient matrix (i.e., the part that is to the left of the vertical bar) is in row echelon form." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186129395 :activity/expected-seconds 420.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

more, with the leading entries highlighted.

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

We say that a matrix is in **row echelon form** if it satisfies the following conditions:

I. - All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.
II. - Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

Here, $B$ is in row echelon form since both conditions are satisfied. However, $A$ is not in row echelon form since condition II is violated: the leading entry of the third row $(a_{32}={\color{red}1})$ is placed just below the leading entry of the second row $(a_{22}=3).$

Students then explore matrices in-depth. They study Gaussian elimination, solve systems of equations, learn about determinants and their properties, and compute inverse matrices. These tools form the computational backbone of many machine learning algorithms.

The course then develops key applications of linear algebra in machine learning. Students also study optimization of multivariable functions, including critical points, second derivative tests, and constrained optimization using Lagrange multipliers. These techniques form the mathematical foundation of algorithms such as support vector machines and constrained optimization problems in machine learning.
Students work with standard multivariable surfaces to build intuition for loss surfaces, and study double integrals as a tool for understanding continuous probability distributions.
On the probability and statistics side, students study discrete and continuous random variables, including probability density functions, cumulative distribution functions, transformations, expectation, moments, variance, and Bayes' theorem.
